responseMessageContents.text:
Looking at your map, there are two issues causing mountains like Everest not to appear:

1. **`mapType="terrain"` is only supported on Google Maps (Android)** — on iOS Apple Maps this is invalid and can cause rendering glitches.
2. **`initialRegion` is centered wrong** — latitude 30 / longitude 10 with delta 120 doesn't actually include Everest (86° E) on most screen aspect ratios, and Apple Maps clamps the delta so Asia gets cut off.

Let me fix both:

responseMessageContents.text: Fixed. The map was centered at longitude 10° with a delta of 120°, which only covered roughly -50° to 70° longitude — so Everest (86° E), K2, Kangchenjunga and all Himalayan peaks were off-screen on initial load. I also switched off `terrain` map type on iOS (Apple Maps doesn't support it) and added `tracksViewChanges={false}` so markers render more reliably. Now the initial view is centered to include the Himalayas, Americas, and Europe.
